lake-tai.name: Lake Tai
lake-tai.bio: The third largest freshwater lake in China, known for its fish and freshwater pearls and lined with scenic areas.
lake-tai.notes: Free/open is not explicitly sourced (lake has no gate; ticketed areas like Yuantouzhu sit on its shore): orchestrator to confirm.

wuxi-2.name: Turtle Head Island
wuxi-2.bio: A peninsula on Lake Tai's northwest shore named for a turtle-shaped rock, known for cherry blossoms in March and April.
wuxi-2.notes: ticketUrl BLOCKED: http://www.ytz.com.cn/ . Price includes ferry. wiki=Yuantouzhu.

wuxi-4.name: Jichang Garden
wuxi-4.bio: A Ming-origin classical garden at the foot of Mount Hui that inspired gardens at the Summer Palace and Yuanming Yuan.
wuxi-4.notes: 70 is the combined Huishan Ancient Town ticket (govt list); Wikivoyage says 65. A 2025-09 notice said the garden was under closed management: check.

wuxi-6.name: Nianhua Bay
wuxi-6.bio: A Zen-themed town scenic area on the Lake Tai shore, just west of the Lingshan Scenic Area in Binhu District.
wuxi-6.notes: Price from Wikivoyage (Oct 2023), guide-level; no official site found.

wuxi-8.name: Liyuan Garden
wuxi-8.bio: A lakeside Chinese garden named for Fan Li, with a 100-year-old white wisteria nicknamed the Money Tree.
wuxi-8.notes: Range is low to high season.

wuxi-10.name: Donglin Academy
wuxi-10.bio: A Northern Song academy founded in 1111, with Ming and Qing halls, a stone arch and a pool.
wuxi-10.notes: Conflict: Wikivoyage says 5 yuan; govt list (Oct 2025) says free, used.

wuxi-12.name: Wuxi Museum
wuxi-12.bio: A museum holding nearly 40,000 relics, from paintings and calligraphy to purple clay teapots and Huishan clay figurines.
wuxi-12.notes: Free per govt list and Wikivoyage.

wuxi-14.name: Dangkou Ancient Town
wuxi-14.bio: A 4A-rated ancient-town scenic area in Ehu town, Xishan District, free to enter.
wuxi-14.notes: Free per govt list; at Ehu town, not Meicun.

wuxi-16.name: Wuxi Zoo
wuxi-16.bio: A zoo and amusement park at the foot of Huishan with over 1,000 rare animals and giant panda research programmes.

wuxi-18.name: Wuxi Sunac Sea World
wuxi-18.bio: A marine park in Binhu with sharks and rays, planned to hold about 1,500 marine species.
wuxi-18.notes: Price guide-level (Wikivoyage Dec 2023); no official site.

wuxi-20.name: Helu City Site
wuxi-20.bio: A museum on the site of King Helu of Wu's capital, housed in a phoenix-shaped building.

yixing-1.name: Yixing Ceramics Museum
yixing-1.bio: One of China's earliest ceramics museums, with 107 relics from Neolithic pottery to Ming and Qing zisha teapots.
yixing-1.notes: Conflict: Wikivoyage free vs govt list 5; govt used.

yixing-3.name: Longchi Mountain Scenic Area
yixing-3.bio: A nature reserve in the Zhangzhu hills with golden pine and magnolia trees unique to China, and a bicycle park.
yixing-3.notes: General entry free; sightseeing car and bike hire extra (Wikivoyage).

yixing-5.name: Zhanggong's Cave
yixing-5.bio: A 4A-rated karst cave scenic area in Zhangyang village in Yixing's Hufu town.
yixing-5.notes: Govt lists as Zhang Daoling's Cave; Taoist claim unverified so omitted.

yixing-7.name: Longbeishan Forest Park
yixing-7.bio: A 4A forest park on Renmin South Road in Yixing city, free to enter.

jiangyin-2.name: Changjing Ancient Town
jiangyin-2.bio: A 3A water town in southeast Jiangyin with canals, old stone streets and over 2,000 years of history.
jiangyin-2.notes: Free, open 24 hours per govt list.

jiangyin-4.name: Ebizui Park
jiangyin-4.bio: A Yangtze riverside park named for its goose's-nose shape, with river views and tree-lined walking paths.
jiangyin-4.notes: Free is medium confidence (govt lists Binjiang Fortress area free; Ctrip for Ebizui itself).
jiangyin-4.held: free not sourced for Ebizui itself

jiangyin-6.name: Former Residence of Liu Brothers
jiangyin-6.bio: The former home of linguist Liu Bannong and erhu composer Liu Tianhua, with six halls on the three Liu brothers.
jiangyin-6.notes: Free per a Ctrip travelogue (c.2020), possibly outdated; low-medium confidence.

wuxi-1.name: Grand Buddha at Ling Shan
wuxi-1.bio: A bronze Buddha statue over 80 m tall at Lingshan on Lake Tai's north shore, one of the largest in China.
wuxi-1.notes: Price 210 is guide-level (Wikivoyage); other sites show 150-210, uncertain.

wuxi-3.name: Xihui Park
wuxi-3.bio: A state park west of Wuxi, set up in 1958, with Jichang Garden, the Second Spring under Heaven and a cable car up Mount Hui.
wuxi-3.notes: Park/old town reported free but main ticket unpriced; merged scenic area with Huishan Ancient Town.

wuxi-5.name: Huishan Ancient Town
wuxi-5.bio: A historic district at the eastern foot of Huishan with traditional streets, old buildings and ancestral halls.
wuxi-5.notes: Free admission per Wikivoyage; Jichang Garden inside is a separate ticket.

wuxi-7.name: Lihu Park
wuxi-7.bio: A free 300-acre park beside Lake Tai in Binhu District, with a Ferris wheel, a carousel and a maze.

wuxi-9.name: Nanchang Street
wuxi-9.bio: A renovated canal street beside Qingming Bridge, the best-kept stretch of Wuxi's traditional canal town.

wuxi-11.name: Plum Garden
wuxi-11.bio: A Lake Tai botanical garden with about 4,000 fruit trees that blossom in spring, beside the old Rong family mansions.
wuxi-11.notes: Price 60 from a search summary of the Wuxi gov/China Daily listing (page not loaded); may rise in blossom season. Research says ~4000 'fruit trees'; bio says plum trees as the garden is named for plums: verify.

wuxi-13.name: Taibo Temple
wuxi-13.bio: A large Ming and Qing temple complex near an ancient town entrance, among the best preserved in Wuxi.

wuxi-15.name: Jin Gui Park
wuxi-15.bio: A 48-hectare park in Binhu District, one of the city's largest, with cherry blossoms and tulips in March and April.
wuxi-15.notes: City park, likely free but unsourced.

wuxi-17.name: Wuxi Sunac Land
wuxi-17.bio: An amusement park in Binhu District with a 1,278 m roller coaster that reaches 118 km/h, reachable by Metro Line 1.
wuxi-17.notes: ticketUrl unverified (candidate domain not recorded); price is guide-level (Wikivoyage Dec 2023).

wuxi-21.name: Hongshan Archaeological Museum
wuxi-21.bio: A museum of the Hongshan archaeological site in Hongshan subdistrict, Xinwu District, free to enter.
wuxi-21.notes: Reservation may still apply (WeChat) - unconfirmed; entry free per 163.com commentary.

yixing-2.name: Yixing Bamboo Sea
yixing-2.bio: A national 4A bamboo forest park in Hufu town, 31 km southwest of Yixing city, among Wuxi's Eighteen Scenic Spots.

yixing-4.name: Shanjuan Cave
yixing-4.bio: A cave in Luoyan Mountain with upper, middle, lower and water caves and a boat ride on an underground river.
yixing-4.notes: Price 145 from Bendibao (undated); adult price unconfirmed by operator.

yixing-6.name: Tuanjiu Scenic Area
yixing-6.bio: A lake scenic area in Yixing rated 4A, with the Yiyuan garden and a plaza and park on its east shore.
yixing-6.notes: Free per Ctrip listings via search summary (pages not loaded).

jiangyin-1.name: Xu Xiake's Former Residence
jiangyin-1.bio: The Ming-style birthplace of travel writer Xu Xiake, with the study where he wrote his Travel Diaries.

jiangyin-3.name: Junshan Park
jiangyin-3.bio: A park that was once a pleasure ground of Wu and Yue nobles, with buildings and inscriptions on Jiangyin's history.

jiangyin-5.name: Huangshan Fort
jiangyin-5.bio: A late Qing fort in the Jiangyin Fortress system, with gun emplacements, underground bunkers and observation posts.
